appraisal_events.evidence: ajouta moitié par méchanceté pour celle-ci... « Pas agréable… pour son mari ! »... dit la princesse qui probablement n'en aurait rien fait si elle avait connu la jeune femme.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly frames the duchesse's remark about Mme de Cambremer as half-spiteful and her offer to introduce her as insincere, locally diminishing Mme de Cambremer while also exposing the duchesse's own hollow politeness.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mais je suis pleine de respect pour les héros, dit la princesse, sur un ton légèrement ironique... je ne connais rien de plus pompier, de plus bourgeois que cet horrible style avec ces commodes qui ont des têtes de cygnes comme des baignoires.
appraisal_events.explanation: Against Froberville's earnest defense of the Iéna family's Empire nobility, the duchesse deploys ironic mock-respect and then openly mocks their furniture and taste as vulgar and bourgeois, locally lowering the Iéna's standing while asserting her own aristocratic authority.

status_effects.explanation: Mme de Cambremer is locally lowered by the duchesse's veiled, malicious insinuation about her forwardness being unbecoming toward her husband.
The narrator's aside that the duchesse would probably not have followed through on her offer exposes her politeness as insincere, mildly undercutting her within this exchange.
The Iéna family's Empire-era nobility and furnishings are locally dismissed as tasteless and bourgeois by the duchesse, lowering their standing relative to old nobility.
The duchesse dominates the exchange with pointed irony and aesthetic authority, deflating Froberville's sincere defense of the Iéna family.

ambiguities: The duchesse's mock-respectful 'je suis pleine de respect pour les héros' is marked as ironic, so it is unclear whether her subsequent diminishment of the Iéna family's taste is a narrator-endorsed judgment or itself a display of her own vanity and snobbery being gently exposed.
